front_blocks.md: Explain how a shoot bends towards a light source.

back_blocks.md: When light shines **predominantly from one side**, auxin made in the tip concentrates on the **shaded side**.
Cells on the shaded side **elongate faster** than those on the sunny side.
This **unequal growth** makes the shoot **bend towards the light**.

This **unequal growth** makes the shoot **bend towards the light**.

back_blocks.md: Auxin is distributed **evenly**, so the cells grow at the **same rate** and the shoot grows straight up.

cards.front_md: What happens if light shines evenly all around a shoot tip?

front_blocks.md: Describe the reflex arc for withdrawing a finger from a hot object.

back_blocks.md: A **receptor** in the skin detects the **stimulus**.
A **sensory neurone** sends impulses to the **spinal cord**, which acts as the co-ordinator.
The impulse passes to a **relay neurone** in the spinal cord.
The relay neurone **synapses** with a **motor neurone**.
The motor neurone carries the impulse to a **muscle** (the **effector**), which **contracts** and pulls the finger away.

back_blocks.md: Sweat only cools the body when it **evaporates**.
In humid air the water vapour cannot escape easily, so evaporation slows and less heat is removed.

front_blocks.md: Give four effects of adrenaline.

back_blocks.md:

- **Breakdown of stored glycogen to glucose** in the liver and muscle cells

front_blocks.md: Where is insulin produced, and what is its role?

back_blocks.md: In the **pancreas**, which acts as an **endocrine gland**.

front_blocks.md: Describe what happens when blood glucose gets too high.

back_blocks.md: Cells in the **pancreas** detect the rise and secrete **insulin** into the blood.
Insulin stimulates the **muscles and liver** to **take up glucose** and store it as **glycogen**.
Blood glucose falls back to normal, and the pancreas stops secreting insulin.
